title: Unveiling the K+-sensitivity of cell metabolism using genetically encoded, FRET-based K+, glucose, and ATP biosensors
protocol: Remove cells cultivated within a 10 cm dish to a confluency of ∼90% from the incubator under sterile conditions.
Dilute Trypsin-EDTA with PBS to a final concentration of 0.05%.
Replace cell culture medium twice with 10 ml pre-warmed PBS.
Remove PBS and add 3 ml of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA in PBS.
Return the cells to the incubator for 2 min to check for detachment.
If cells have not detached after 5 min, continue incubating at 37°C and check every minute.
Stop trypsinization by adding 10 ml of pre-warmed complemented medium (DMEM + 10% FCS + penicillin-streptomycin + sodium pyruvate).
Transfer the cells to a 15 ml conical tube and pellet them at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant from the cells without disturbing the cell pellet.
Fully resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of complemented medium (DMEM + 10% FCS + 1× penicillin-streptomycin + 1× sodium pyruvate).
Count the cells using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber or another method, using 15 μL of cell suspension for one chamber.
Count cells in two chambers by determining the number of total cells in four large squares per chamber and dividing this number by 4.
Take the average of the counts from the two chambers.
Multiply the average count by 10,000 to determine the cell number/mL.
Seed HEK293 cells into desired wells in a 6-well plate containing 30 mm circular glass coverslips.
Cultivate the cells for 16–24 hours.
Place 30 mm circular glass coverslips in the desired number of wells in 6-well plates.
Add 1 mL of complemented medium (DMEM + 10% FCS, + penicillin/streptomycin, + 1× sodium pyruvate) to each well.
Push the coverslips to the bottom of the 6-well plate with a sterile pipette tip to ensure they firmly stick.
Dilute HEK293 cells to 600,000 cells/mL.
Add 500 μL of the cell suspension to each well of the 6-well plate containing glass coverslips.
Ensure the final culture volume per well is 1.5 mL.
Place the 6-well plates in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 16–24 hours.
Perform a medium change on cells seeded the day before.
Transfect HEK293 cells with sensor plasmids using PolyJet transfection reagent.
Remove the cells from the incubator and check their morphology, density, and for possible bacterial or fungal contaminations using a cell culture microscope.
If transfection is planned for the next day, HEK293 cells should show a density of approximately 40%–50% on the day of transfection.

Remove the medium from each well that will be transfected with a sensor plasmid and carefully add 1 mL of fresh and prewarmed complemented medium (DMEM + 10% FCS, + penicillin/streptomycin, + 1× sodium pyruvate) to each well.
Return the cells to the incubator for 30 min after changing the medium.
Prepare the transfection mixture using the plasmid of choice and PolyJet transfection reagent approximately 20 minutes after returning the cells to the incubator.
For each well that will be transfected with a plasmid, prepare 50 μL of FCS-free DMEM medium.
If two 6-well plates are being transfected with different probes (probe A and B), prepare 2 × 300 μL of serum-free DMEM in separate tubes for each probe.
Add 1.0 μg of plasmid DNA per transfected well to the prepared transfection mixture.
For mitochondria-targeted constructs, reduce the amount of DNA to 0.3 μg/well to ensure proper mitochondrial targeting of the probes.
Prepare 50 μL of FCS-free DMEM in a separate tube for each well to be transfected.
Pipette 3 μL of PolyJet transfection reagent into the tube for each well that will be transfected.
Mix the contents of the tube containing the PolyJet transfection reagent by pipetting.
Prepare the DNA-containing medium mixture and place it in a separate tube (tube A).
Mix the DNA-medium mixture from tube A with an equal volume of the PolyJet-media mixture from tube C thoroughly by pipetting.
Incubate the combined DNA-transfection mixture for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove cells from the incubator and add 100 μL of each transfection mixture drop-by-drop to each well that should be transfected with the respective probe.
Return the cells to the incubator and incubate them at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 12–16 hours.
Prepare the transfection mixture in FCS-free medium.
Incubate the transfection mixture without perturbations to allow complex formation.
Remove cells from the incubator on the day of the experiment.
Replace the transfection mixture with cell equilibration buffer.
Warm PBS and cell-equilibration buffer to 37°C using a water bath.
Check morphology, density, and possible contaminations under a microscope.
Exchange the medium in the cells for cell-equilibration buffer.
Remove all medium from the cells.
Add 1.5 ml of PBS per well to remove residual medium.
Carefully remove the PBS after addition.
Add 1.5 ml of cell-equilibration buffer per well.
Keep cells in the dark at 20°C–25°C until measurement.
Pre-equilibrate cells for at least 30 minutes before measurement.
Complement the buffers with the required compounds.
Pre-warm nutrient-free imaging buffer to 20°C–25°C.
Aliquot 200 mL of buffer in a new bottle without adding additional compounds (= IB -GLU).
Add 10 mM of d-glucose to the residual 800 mL of buffer (= IB + GLU).
Aliquot 200 mL of basal imaging buffer in a new bottle and add 3-BP at a final concentration of 300 μM (= IB + 3-BP) from a 300 mM H2O stock (1:1000 dilution).

Aliquot 200 mL of basal imaging buffer in a new bottle and add oligomycin-A at a final concentration of 3 μM and antimycin-A at a final concentration of 5 μM (= IB + O/A) from 10 mM DMSO stocks, respectively (1:3333 and 1:2000 dilutions).
Aliquot 200 mL of basal imaging buffer in a new bottle and add gramicidin at a final concentration of 15 μM (= IB + GRAM) from a 15 mM DMSO stock (1:1000 dilution).
Mix buffers with glucose and metabolic modulators on the day of imaging experiments.
Start the PC and open the perfusion system software to prepare the perfusion system.
Wash the perfusion system with 10 mL of 70% ethanol in each syringe.
Add 20 mL of ddH2O per syringe to remove residual ethanol.
Close the valves of the perfusion system using the perfusion system software.
Prepare the system with selected buffers, filling one buffer in each syringe.
Shorten open the valves of the perfusion system to remove air from the tubings.
Repeat washing steps with 70% ethanol and ddH2O in the cleaning channel.
Remove all air from the tubes and clean the system.
Open the channel containing the “basal buffer” (IB + GLU).
Adjust the flow rate of the perfusion system to approximately 1 mL/min using tube clamps.
Close all valves in the software to stop perfusion.
Open the imaging software and adjust the imaging parameters.
Use a binning of 4, LED intensity at 455 nm of ∼1%–2%, exposure time of ∼200 ms, and interval time of ∼3 s as starting points for the microscope setup.
Adjust the settings of the microscope for simultaneous detection of CFP- and FRET emission upon excitation with the 455 nm LED and the 427/10 excitation filter.
Minimize light intensities to prevent phototoxic effects and photobleaching.
Increase camera binning to yield higher fluorescence emission signals from cells while keeping excitation light intensities low.
Adjust imaging intervals based on the expected duration of the experiment to prevent phototoxic effects and photobleaching.
Use imaging parameters adjusted for each sensor without changing them when measuring the same sensor on different days to ensure consistency.
On Day 3, after cell equilibration in the buffer for 30 minutes, start experiments by carefully transferring a glass coverslip containing cells from a 6-well plate to the perfusion chamber.
Use a 25G needle and sharp forceps or a commercially available lens lifter for coverslip transfer.
Ensure that no edge of the coverslip is damaged during transfer.
Place the coverslip in the notch of the lower part of the perfusion chamber.
Insert the sealing ring into the upper part of the chamber.
Close the perfusion chamber by placing the upper part on top of the lower part.
Add 1 mL of cell equilibration buffer to hydrate the cells.
Remove excess buffer with a paper towel.
Check the tightness of the perfusion chamber using a dry paper towel around the glass coverslip edge.
Place the perfusion chamber on top of the microscope.
Start perfusing the cells with IB + GLU.
If using an oil immersion objective, add a drop of fluorescence-suitable immersion oil to the objective.
Attach the tube of the perfusion system to the inlet of the perfusion chamber.
Open the valve of IB + GLU buffer to start perfusing the cells.
Check for functional perfusion by observing an increase in volume within the chamber.
Attach the tube of the vacuum pump to the outlet of the chamber.
Screen the coverslip for a suitable imaging section with cells showing good signal-to-noise ratio and proper targeting of the respective fluorescent probe.
Ensure correct targeting of fluorescent probes mtAT1.03 and mt lc-LysM GEPII 1.0 to the mitochondrial matrix.
Perform a preliminary experiment to test for correct targeting and expression of the sensor.
Avoid using too high DNA or PolyJet transfection reagent concentrations, which can cause excessive mistargeting.
Ensure cell confluency within the area of interest is not too high to prevent slower cell responses due to limited buffer/compound diffusion.
Start imaging experiments on Day 3, approximately 25 minutes per experiment.
Select cells suitable for imaging based on correct targeting and expression of sensors.
Follow the fluorescence over-time of CFP- and FRET emissions in selected cells.
Set distinct light intensity, exposure time, binning, and interval for recording images.
Do not select the brightest cells to maintain consistent settings across experiments.
Measure average fluorescence intensities representative of the whole population.
Draw regions of interest around every cell of interest.
Include one background region without fluorescence signal from neighboring cells.
Record baseline fluorescence intensities in IB+GLU buffer for 5 min.
Switch to experimental buffers containing no glucose, 3 μM oligomycin-A and 5 μM antimycin-A, 300 μM 3-BP, or 15 μM gramicidin after the initial recording period.
Record fluorescence over-time values for at least 10 min until ratio stabilizes.
Repeat steps a-e for cells transfected with each sensor (mtAT1.03, FLII12Pglu-700μδ6, NES lc-LysM GEPII 1.0, and mt lc-LysM GEPII 1.0) at least five times on three different days.
Ensure consistent settings for each sensor across all experiments.
Stop the image acquisition.
Export the fluorescence over-time values to Microsoft Excel.
Stop the perfusion system.
Withdraw the coverslip and extensively wash the perfusion system with ethanol.
Wash the chamber with ddH2O.
Start the next experiment by repeating steps 7–9.
Correct the fluorescence over-time values of every cell measured for background intensity.
Subtract the fluorescence over-time of the cyan channel from the CFP signal of the cells.
Subtract the fluorescence over-time values of the FRET-channel from the FRET signal of the cells.
Calculate the FRET-ratio signal by dividing the background-corrected values of FRET/CFP.
Plot the FRET-ratio signal over-time.
Use the one phase decay function provided by GraphPad Prism to correct for photobleaching.
Normalize the FRET-ratio signal data over time by dividing R by the R0 function (Figure 4B).
Check the bleaching correction for correctness.
Plot the average of the normalized [GLU]cyto response over the average of the normalized [ATP]mito alteration for each treatment.
Subtract 1 from both average responses to obtain the net change from basal values.
Represent results by plotting averaged [GLU]cyto over [ATP]mito after baseline subtraction.
Plot the average of the normalized [K+]cyto alteration over the average of the normalized [K+]mito alteration for each treatment.
Subtract the value “1” from both averages to yield the net change of [K+]cyto and [K+]mito from the basal value.
Check the correctness of the photobleaching correction procedure by comparing uncorrected raw curves/responses with corrected curves.
Double-check curve fitting to avoid over- or underestimation of responses/effects.
Test other corrections than one-phase-decay in case of bad fitting.
Ensure thorough and exact timing for experiments.
Follow identical schedules for total duration and superfusion procedures across all measurements.
